question: What makes ticket B's native hybrid paths work: is hybridness necessary, does nativeness transport, and which cells remember?

public_inputs.library: experiments/PATH-HYBRID-20261108-001B/PATH-HYBRID-20261108-001B-E001_hybrid_middles/hybrid_lib.py (sha256 18643b53edb2043060713c3d618f6c5685941f7cd56d80dacf970e9de6c86eb0); GROWTH-LAW-20261107-001A's generic enumerator and knotlab check for the canonical check.
public_inputs.paths: artifacts/PATH-HYBRID-20261108-001B/PATH-HYBRID-20261108-001B-E001_hybrid_middles/run/paths.json (sha256 c647436f3c56b1bb5ca2af503bc68da57e43fafeae8874ef4dfc57e62c0ca0b5): ticket B's paths with all three contacts persistent; its 1,120 native ones are measured.
public_inputs.run: run.py in this folder, 16 worker processes.
public_inputs.measures: (1) each native path with ring C made uniform under each of the 8 linear rules; (2) ring C grown by one cell on the far side of c3, with the rule of either neighbour, and rings A or D grown by one cell; (3) the ring-C cells whose first rows stay in c3's eventual support; (4) for the smallest native path, the knots of c3's two-time law at lags L to L + 5 by the generic enumerator, and knotlab check on the parity of c3's eventual support.

forbidden_inputs: Changing the measures after seeing results
primary_observable: How many native paths need hybridness; how often nativeness survives one more cell; the canonical check.
cheapest_meaningful_control: The canonical check must find, at every lag from L on, knots through c3(T) that meet all four rings.
decision_or_followup_rule: No frozen hypothesis beyond the control: report the measures. If every native path needs hybridness, record that uniform second middle rings did not give native paths here.
stop_rule: Stop when the measures are computed.
feasibility_disclosure: Before freezing: ticket B's result and interpretation had been read. No measure was computed.
